subject: MSA / Order Form — DPA scope boundary and hosting jurisdiction questions
messages:
From: Emma Gardner <emma.gardner@cloudhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@cloudhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA redline + hosting jurisdiction questions

Sofia — thanks for sending the draft. We reviewed the DPA and have two quick asks before we send to procurement for sign-off:

1) Hosting / jurisdiction boundary: your current order form references ‘hosting in EU regions’ but the DPA’s transfer routing language is broad. Can you confirm whether any processing or backups for CloudHealth customer data may touch non-EU territories (US/SG)? We need to confirm the applicability of SCCs vs. Transfer Impact Addendum.

2) Controller/Processor mapping: the Order Form includes an analytics feature (Insights) that indicates Redwood will run transient model-training on aggregated usage. Please confirm whether you treat aggregated analytics and model tuning as Processor activities under the DPA or something else — our counsel wants to ensure no change in legal status.

Attaching our redline (CloudHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and a hosting matrix for our current deployment topology. Can your team confirm by EOD Tues (PDT)?

Best,
Emma Gardner
Senior Counsel, CloudHealth Ltd.
attachments: CloudHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx (docx), hosting_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Emma Gardner <emma.gardner@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redline + hosting jurisdiction questions

Emma — thanks, received. Looping in Ben (sales) and Laura/Irène on legal/hosting. Quick summary from our side below; we’ll follow up with a short note that legal can rely on for procurement.

- Hosting territories: Production serving and KV cache for EU customers will be pinned to EU regions (Frankfurt / Amsterdam) per the Order Form. However, for resilience we do replicate encrypted backups to a cross-region S3 bucket that sits in the US (us-east-1) for disaster recovery — that can be scoped as an export under SCCs. We can add an explicit hosting appendix outlining which artifacts are EU-only vs. cross-region.

- Analytics & model tuning: Redwood’s Insights pipeline receives metadata and aggregated usage metrics. We confirm that Insights ingestion is treated as Processor activity; we do not use raw customer content for model re-training without an explicit opt-in and separate agreement. We can add a carve-out clause clarifying this.

Action: Laura/Irène — can you validate the proposed wording for a hosting appendix and a short opt-in carve-out for model tuning? Ben, I’ll need a quick note on commercial impact if we include a cross-region backup restriction.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redline + hosting jurisdiction questions

Sofia — thanks for the summary. I reviewed CloudHealth’s redline and propose the following (high level):

1) Hosting appendix: Add a short table to the Order Form / Annex showing (a) production serving region(s) (EU-FRA, EU-AMS), (b) backup/resilience replication (US - us-east-1) and (c) logs/metrics retention location (EU). Add explicit language that backups are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys available for enterprise plans. This limits surprises for procurement.

2) Transfer legal text: Keep SCCs as the primary governance mechanism. Add an explicit mention that backups and DR replicas are covered by SCCs and the Transfer Impact Assessment we performed (attach TIA summary). If CloudHealth insists on EU-only backups we can discuss a billing addendum for restricted replication.

3) Model tuning: Accept the Processor-only approach. Add a one-sentence carve-out: ‘Redwood will only use aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry for model tuning and will not use Customer Content for model training absent written opt-in and an additional agreement.’

Irene — can you draft the hosting appendix and the one-sentence carve-out? I’ll prepare the legal wording for the SCCs + TIA reference.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Emma Gardner <emma.gardner@cloudhealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redline + hosting jurisdiction questions

Emma — draft hosting appendix and short carve-out below (copied into this email so it can be pasted into the Order Form/Annex):

--- START HOSTING APPENDIX (DRAFT) ---
Hosting appendix (Order Form Annex A):
- Production serving region(s): EU - Frankfurt (eu-central-1) and EU - Amsterdam (eu-west-1).
- Backups / DR replication: Encrypted replicas stored in us-east-1 for disaster recovery. Replicas are encrypted with server-side encryption by default; customer-managed KMS available on Enterprise plans.
- Logs and aggregated metrics: Retained within EU regions for EU customers; exported metadata used for monitoring and capacity planning is pseudonymized and stored in EU.
--- END HOSTING APPENDIX ---

--- START MODEL TUNING CARVE-OUT (DRAFT) ---
Redwood will process aggregated and pseudonymized telemetry and metadata for the purpose of service improvement and model tuning. Redwood will not use Customer Content (as defined in the MSA) for model training, tuning, or improvement without Customer’s prior written consent and a separate agreement that specifies scope and controls.
--- END CARVE-OUT ---

If that looks okay to CloudHealth I’ll generate a tracked-change version against their redline.

Irene Choi
Privacy & Trust, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Gardner <emma.gardner@cloudhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redline + hosting jurisdiction questions

Thanks — that is very helpful and addresses most of our concerns. Two follow ups:

1) Can you add a sentence in the hosting appendix that backups are retained for a maximum of 30 days in us-east-1 unless otherwise agreed? That will keep our security team comfortable.

2) For the model-tuning carve-out: we would like a confirmation that pseudonymization is irreversible (e.g., keys or mapping are never stored in a way that would allow re-identification). If Redwood cannot confirm irreversibility, we’ll need a stronger opt-in gating mechanism.

If you can update the appendix with the 30-day retention cap and add a short sentence on pseudonymization practice I can circulate the tracked redline to procurement and we’ll aim to get to signature next week.

Best,
Emma
Senior Counsel, CloudHealth Ltd.
